Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants using speaker equipment are advised to use handset mode for improved audio quality. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Thornton, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Development Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Solara Renewables had a strong Q3, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements. First, our overall performance highlights and key achievements stand out. We delivered exceptional results across the board at Solara Renewables, fueled by strong project execution, supportive policies like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act's Section 45X manufacturing credits and the EU's Net-Zero Industry Act, and our disciplined approach to costs as LCOE for solar and wind dips below $25 per MWh in top U.S. markets.

Revenue jumped 28 percent year-over-year to $1.2 billion, exceeding our guidance and extending our streak of robust growth. Utility-scale solar drove much of this with a significant ramp-up, fueled by hyperscaler PPAs from partners like Google and Microsoft. Wind and hybrid projects contributed strongly, while energy storage solutions saw explosive growth from BESS paired with solar-plus-storage systems. We're now guiding full-year revenue toward the higher end, around $4.8 billion, with adjusted EBITDA margins reaching 28 percent—a substantial improvement—due to economies of scale and gross margins at a five-year high of 28.5 percent.

Our development pipeline expanded to 50.7 GW total, with 18.2 GW in late-stage development and a $18.5 billion backlog up sharply year-over-year, offering clear visibility into 2028 at attractive 12 to 14 percent unlevered IRRs, on par with leaders like NextEra and Orsted.

Key wins included bringing our 450 MW Desert Sun solar project in California's CAISO market online early and under budget, using TOPCon bifacial modules at 23.2 percent efficiency for a 15-year PPA at $22 per MWh, avoiding 650,000 tons of CO2 yearly—akin to removing 140,000 vehicles from roads. U.S. operations now make up 62 percent of revenue, enhanced by over $45 million in Q3 IRA domestic content credits.

In wind, Phase 1 of our 320 MW onshore farm in ERCOT Texas went live with 150 MW/600 MWh LFP storage, hitting 48 percent capacity factor and a 20-year PPA at $28 per MWh with a major industrial buyer. Internationally, our 200 MW offshore stake in the North Sea's Hollandse Kust Noord cluster reached full COD with Vestas 15 MW turbines, leveraging EU subsidies.

Storage shone with 1.2 GWh deployed, highlighted by a 400 MW/1.6 GWh system in Arizona using LFP cells from our CATL JV, capitalizing on ERCOT spreads and ancillary services for 18 percent IRRs. Our clean tech pilots advanced a 50 MW green hydrogen electrolyzer in Australia for miners and next-gen flow batteries at 95 percent efficiency.

These reflect our hub-and-spoke model, centralizing EPC at our 2 GW Texas hub at 85 percent utilization to cut BOS costs 22 percent, with spokes localizing in Europe and APAC. ESG progress includes 2.1 million tCO2e avoided YTD, progress toward SBTi 50 percent Scope 1 and 2 cuts by 2030, and an MSCI ESG AA rating. Supply chain pressures on trackers and inverters are hedged via 18-month contracts and integration.

Second, gross margin and operating margin trends showed solid expansion. We achieved a non-GAAP gross margin of 28.5 percent, up 320 basis points year-over-year and 110 sequentially, marking six straight quarters of gains and a trailing 12-month average of 27.1 percent—beating Tier-1 solar benchmarks from BloombergNEF.

This stemmed from solar PV cost drops, with polysilicon at $8.5 per kg flowing to TOPCon n-type BOMs at $0.22 per Wp. Premium mix shifts to 23.5 percent efficient monofacial TOPCon at 65 percent of shipments added 12 percent ASP uplift to $0.32 per Wp, while BESS LFP packs at 92 percent efficiency grabbed 18 percent premiums.

North America led at 32 percent margins via IRA 45X credits adding 400 bps, Europe at 29 percent from Net-Zero Act support, and APAC steady at 24 percent through 60 percent India localization. Freight hikes and wafer issues were offset by 80 percent poly-Si hedging at $9 per kg and 70 percent upstream control.

Operating margins hit 12.3 percent, up 250 bps YoY, with TTM at 11.5 percent. OpEx at $156 million or 18.2 percent of revenue improved 120 bps, R&D up 15 percent to $42 million for perovskite tandems targeting 30 percent efficiency and electrolyzers, SG&A flat at 7.1 percent via efficiencies. U.S. OpEx lean at 15 percent, APAC sub-14 percent, Europe 22 percent countered by automation.

We're targeting 32 percent gross and 16 percent op margins by FY2025 via 12 GW offtake at 30-plus percent blended, 15 GW solar fab expansion, and 2 GWh BESS line, riding 25 percent global BESS CAGR.

Third, our capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets remain robust. We ended Q3 with 12.4 GW operating—up 28 percent YoY—including 8.2 GW solar PV, 3.5 GW onshore wind, 0.5 GW offshore, and 200 MWh BESS.

Full-year 2024 guidance holds at 1.8 GW additions, up 35 percent from 2023, via two 400 MW Southwest solar farms with TOPCon bifacials, a 500 MW Texas onshore wind with Vestas V236-15.0s, and a 300 MW India hybrid with HJT and 150 MWh LFP.

For 2025, we're guiding 2.9 GW gross additions—a 61 percent increase—for a 48 percent CAGR to 25 GW operating by decade-end, scaling to 4-5 GW annually from 2026 per IEA trends.

Pipeline totals 50.7 GW: 18.2 GW late-stage, 32.5 GW early, 62 percent conversion. Solar 65 percent or 33 GW with tandems; wind 25 percent or 12.7 GW onshore/offshore; storage/hybrids 10 percent or 5 GW/2.5 GWh.

Regions: North America 42 percent or 21.4 GW with IRA unlocks; Europe 28 percent or 14.2 GW under REPowerEU; APAC 20 percent or 10.1 GW via India PLI, Australia RES; LatAm/other 10 percent.

Initiatives include $250 million AI O&M for yield gains, M&A adding 2.1 GW at 8x multiples, partnerships with Fluence/LONGi, and green bond financing at 4.2 percent. ROIC 9-11 percent, IRR 12.5 percent, buffered by liquidity.

Fourth, debt levels and financing costs reflect prudent management. Total gross debt was $5.2 billion as of September 30, up 8 percent YoY from new project financings like Hornsea Extend offshore and Gemini hybrid. Net debt at $4.1 billion after $1.1 billion cash, yielding 3.4x net debt-to-EBITDA—better than 3.8x last year and peers like Orsted or NextEra.

Debt mix: 62 percent long-term fixed-rate non-recourse project finance, e.g., $450 million green loan for Texas BESS; 25 percent corporate term/revolvers with $1.2 billion undrawn sustainability-linked; 13 percent green bonds including €500 million 20-year at 3.8 percent.

Cost of debt at 4.2 percent weighted average, down 20 bps QoQ and 60 bps YoY; all-in 4.5 percent via $1.7 billion refinancings swapping to fixed. U.S. 55 percent leverages IRA tax equity; Europe 30 percent EU Taxonomy; APAC 15 percent hedged to 5.2 percent.

Hedging covers 92 percent variable, greenium saves 25 bps, asset rotations recycle $400 million. Leverage to dip below 3.2x year-end, costs to 4.0 percent in 2025 with $2 billion shelf.

Fifth, our strategic priorities and outlook position us strongly. Wrapping up a transformative Q3 with 28 percent revenue growth to $1.2 billion from 600W+ TOPCon bifacials and 45 percent BESS backlog surge, we're focused on scalable solutions amid electrification and decarbonization.

Priority one: U.S. manufacturing scale-up via IRA 45X/45Z, with Phase 2 Texas gigafactory for 10 GW N-type/HJT by mid-2025, plus 5 GW Arizona at 95 percent utilization. Q4 CapEx $450 million funded by $2.8 billion liquidity, targeting 32 percent EBITDA margins, 4.2 GW PPAs with hyperscalers in ERCOT/PJM.

Priority two: BESS leadership with 6-hour LFP at 15 percent higher cycles, 2.5 GWh in California LCFS; $300 million R&D for 100-hour iron-air with Form Energy partners, 1 GWh Australia EPC.

Priority three: Offshore wind/green H2 in Europe/APAC—1.2 GW North Sea with Orsted, €300 billion REPowerEU; 2 GW Gujarat electrolyzers at $1.5/kg for 500 MW pipeline.

Priority four: Digital/ESG with $150 million AssetPerfAI boosting uptime to 99.2 percent, LCOE down 12 percent; SBTi 1.5°C, Scope 3 down 22 percent, CDP A-List.

Q4 revenue $1.35-1.45 billion, EBITDA $380-410 million; FY25 $5.8-6.2 billion, 12 GW solar EPC, 5 GWh BESS, 2 GW wind/H2, 90 percent FCF conversion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Thornton to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue reached $1.2 billion, representing a 28 percent increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 28.5 percent, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $156 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $290 million, or $1.85 per share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Now, I'll pass the call to Sarah Kline to discuss our project development pipeline.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 18.2 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management, including Scope 3 reductions of 22 percent through recycled PV glass and 100 percent renewable-powered factories. We're on track for SBTi-validated 1.5-degree pathways, have avoided 2.1 million tons of CO2 equivalent year-to-date, and earned a CDP A-List rating alongside NextEra, plus MSCI AA. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that our sustainability efforts not only benefit the environment but also create long-term value for our stakeholders.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will be conducting a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Green Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Sarah Kline:
Thanks for the question, John. Supply chain constraints remain a challenge across the industry, particularly with polysilicon volatility, freight disruptions from the Red Sea, and OEM delays on turbines and trackers. However, we've proactively mitigated these through our vertical integration—controlling 70 percent of the upstream chain from ingots to modules—strategic hedging like 80 percent of 2024 poly-Si at $9 per kg and 18 months on BOS components, and reshoring via U.S.-Mexico manufacturing hubs under IRA incentives. Our Texas gigafactory at 85 percent utilization and JVs like CATL for LFP have slashed lead times by 22 percent YoY. For offshore, partnerships with Vestas and Nordex include buffer clauses, keeping our on-time delivery at 95 percent. We've built 24-month construction pads and derisked via M&A of distressed assets. Overall, these have kept our 1.8 GW 2024 additions on track, with minimal slippage expected.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with RenewTech Securities. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Emerging markets are key to our 25 percent CAGR target, and we're approaching them with localized, de-risked plays. In APAC, we're countering India's PLI competition by setting up 2 GW electrolyzer production in Gujarat for green H2 at 70 percent PEM efficiency and $1.5 per kg costs, supporting our 500 MW pipeline doubling YoY per IEA's 80 million ton demand by 2030. Australia's NEM sees our 1 GWh BESS EPC and 2 GW hybrids for 82 percent RES goals, navigating grid bottlenecks with flow batteries. In Europe, REPowerEU's €300 billion drives 1.2 GW North Sea offshore with Orsted floating tech and €800 million Q4 bookings via UK CfD. LatAm leverages Brazil auction wins for 1.5 GW hydro-hybrids with BNDES at 12 percent IRRs. We blend 60 percent localization, IFC guarantees, cross-currency hedges, and policy-tied PPAs—75 percent IG financed—to cap costs and hedge volatility, ensuring ROIC above 9 percent.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Rodriguez with EcoInvest Advisors. Please go ahead.

David Rodriguez:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Elena Vasquez:
Competition is intensifying, David, but we differentiate through tech leadership, scale, and bankable execution. Our TOPCon/HJT modules at 23.5-28 percent efficiencies and proprietary LFP with 15 percent higher cycles outpace commoditized PERC and standard packs, commanding 12-18 percent ASP premiums. AssetPerfAI drives 99.2 percent uptime and 12 percent LCOE cuts on 3 GW assets, like Enphase but utility-scale. Hyperscaler PPAs—4.2 GW up 60 percent QoQ—lock visibility at $18.5 billion backlog, 2.5x FY25 coverage. IRA domestic bonuses, 70/30 import/domestic mix, and greenium financing at 25 bps discounts beat pure-play importers. M&A at 8x multiples, vertical EPC hubs cutting costs 22 percent, and 62 percent pipeline conversion keep us ahead of Invenergy or Adani peers. With $2.8 billion liquidity and 3.4x leverage, we're funding $2.8 billion CapEx for 30 percent growth while peers grapple rates.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Solara Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
